patch.value: GH-1677: the stale-revision refusal's next_steps and examples drop --pm-path, --no-extensions and the output mode, so the recovery reads return another tracker's item

GitHub issue #1677 (reported 2026-11-06 against 2026.11.5 from an agent-UX review). The expected-revision write guard (pm-gh1576) correctly refuses a stale write with item_revision_conflict (exit 4), but its required, examples and next_steps are rendered as pm get <id> --json and pm history <id> --limit 5 with no tracker scope. When the caller selected a tracker with --pm-path (or --path) and --no-extensions, replaying the emitted next_steps reads the cwd tracker instead. In the reporter's two-tracker repro (same id in both), the emitted get returns the DECOY item with a hash different from current_revision and the emitted history returns the decoy's create-only stream: two wasted reads (1,529 B) that look successful. The history step also drops JSON mode. recovery.attempted_command and normalized_args keep the correct scope, so only the prescribed follow-ups are wrong. Cause: assertRevisionEntries in src/core/store/item-mutation-precondition.ts builds the commands deep in the store layer, which never sees the invocation's global options; enrichInvocationRevisionError in src/cli/expected-revisions.ts adds change evidence but does not rescope the commands. Every guarded verb (update, mutate, comments, files, close, release) shares this refusal. Expected: read-only recovery commands carry the invocation's tracker scope (resolvePmCommandScopeArgs: --pm-path spelling and --no-extensions) and the requested output encoding. The guard keeps refusing and never replaces the stale hash or retries the write itself. SDK callers that passed an explicit pmRoot get the same scoped commands. Duplicate check: searched revision conflict next_steps pm-path; pm-mrvq8u (closed) covered revision-conflict follow-ups from the PR 1654 review, not scope; GH-1364 and GH-1386 (closed) own projection-correction retries. This is the revision guard's evidence recovery.

An item_revision_conflict refusal raised by a CLI invocation that selected a tracker with --pm-path or --path renders required, examples and next_steps with that tracker scope and --no-extensions when given; The recovery commands keep the invocation's requested output mode (JSON when --json was given, the default encoding otherwise); The guard still refuses with exit 4, never replaces the expected hash and never retries the write; SDK withExpectedItemRevisions callers that passed an explicit pmRoot receive the same scoped commands; A two-tracker spec with the same id in both executes the emitted next_steps and asserts they read the target tracker's item and history (current_revision matches); Negative control: reverting to unscoped commands fails that spec
Revision-conflict recovery reads carry the invocation's tracker scope and output mode, so replaying them returns the refused item's current revision

value.text: Implementation evidence (branch fix/recovery-replays-invocation). The store-layer refusal (assertRevisionEntries in src/core/store/item-mutation-precondition.ts) now builds required/examples/nextSteps through itemRevisionConflictGuidance and records reason revision_changed or document_unreadable. scopeItemRevisionConflict in src/sdk/lifecycle/item-revision.ts re-renders those fields for an invocation ({scopeArgs, json}). It runs inside enrichItemRevisionConflict, so it also covers refusals that already carry change evidence, and it skips close's post-close fan-out report (reason post_close_auto_unblock_refused, already scoped by commandScope). Hosts: the CLI binds invocationRevisionRecovery(globalOptions) (resolvePmCommandScopeArgs: --pm-path spelling, PM_PATH when not the cwd default, --no-extensions, and JSON when --json or --output-format json) at both preAction bind sites in src/cli/main.ts. SDK withExpectedItemRevisions adds --pm-path for an explicit pmRoot or cwd, PmClient.withExpectedItemRevisions always names its tracker, and runAction/MCP pass resolvePmCommandScopeArgs(global). Verified with the reporter's two-tracker shape: the emitted next_steps now read the target item at current_revision, and the history step returns the target's stream (total 2) in the caller's output mode. The guard still exits 4 and writes nothing. Negative control: dropping the invocation from enrichInvocationRevisionError fails tests/integration/recovery-replays-invocation.integration.spec.ts.

patch.value: next_steps, examples and required name --pm-path and --no-extensions as the caller gave them, plus --json when requested. Replaying them returns the refused item at current_revision, and the guard still refuses with exit 4 without writing.

Revision refusals built in the store layer now record a reason (revision_changed or document_unreadable) and their guidance through itemRevisionConflictGuidance. scopeItemRevisionConflict re-renders that guidance for an invocation. The CLI binds the invocation's resolvePmCommandScopeArgs and JSON mode. SDK withExpectedItemRevisions with an explicit pmRoot or cwd, PmClient.withExpectedItemRevisions, and runAction/MCP pass their tracker scope. Close's post-close fan-out report keeps its own scoped commands.

Verified with the reporter's two-tracker shape (same id in a decoy and a target tracker). The emitted get returned the target item with item_hash equal to current_revision and the edited description. The emitted history returned the target stream (total 2) in JSON, and the TOON refusal emits TOON reads. Removing the invocation from the CLI enrichment fails tests/integration/cli/recovery-replays-invocation.integration.spec.ts (negative control). Full suite 12112 passed, coverage 100/100/100/100.
A stale-revision refusal's read-only recovery now carries the caller's tracker scope, extension isolation and output mode, so replaying it reads the refused item

value.text:
Codex review (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) on PR #1680 head b0a334fa1: 2 findings on this item, both verified and fixed.
(P2) Nested scopes: an outer clientA.withExpectedItemRevisions re-rendered (and added evidence to) a refusal raised by an inner clientB scope on another tracker. The guard now records the canonical tracker of each refusal it raises (itemRevisionRefusalTracker in src/core/store/item-mutation-precondition.ts), and re-created errors keep it (retainItemRevisionRefusalTracker). enrichItemRevisionConflict returns a refusal from another tracker unchanged, so the owning scope supplies both its evidence and its scoped commands.
(P2) runAction with an explicit cwd rendered the caller's relative path, which names another tracker from the caller's process cwd. It now renders the resolved tracker root, including when cwd alone selected the tracker.
Specs: a two-tracker nested-scope case and a runAction explicit-cwd case in tests/unit/sdk/lifecycle/item-revision.spec.ts.

value.text:
Review round 2 on PR #1680 head dc8cad9be (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, 4 findings; CodeRabbit full review, 6 findings). Fixed:
(1) Refusal ownership is shared across SDK bundle graphs through the global registry (Symbol.for @unbrained/pm-cli/item-revision-refusal-trackers), like the scope registry.
(2) Ownership is recovered from the cause chain, so a composition wrapper (finishComposition) still belongs to the inner tracker.
(3) PmClient recovery keeps --no-extensions for a client created with noExtensions true. An active-extension-host client, which disables extensions only internally, does not get it.
(4) The output encoding is explicit. ItemRevisionRecoveryInvocation.outputArgs replaces the json flag, the CLI renders --output-format <fmt> ahead of --json (the canonical flag wins, as for the invocation's own output), and runAction carries a requested outputFormat.
(5) Close's post-close fan-out report now renders its examples with commandScope instead of inheriting the store refusal's unscoped reads.
(6) docs/COMMANDS.md now says the recovery reads are live, not pinned to current_revision.
Not changed: CodeRabbit's note that the pm package manage freshness check should distrust the registry record. That concerns package management, not this change; the record was written by pm package install of 2026.11.5 in this branch.
Full suite 12118 passed, coverage 100/100/100/100.

value.text: Review round 3 on PR #1680 head 6107aeac8 (Codex): runAction derived --no-extensions from the global options of an active-extension-host client, which disables extensions only internally. Replaying the recovery would then hide extension item types. revisionRecoveryScopeArgs in src/sdk/runtime.ts now excludes that internal flag, the same exclusion PmClient.withExpectedItemRevisions uses. The spec drives PmClient.forActiveExtensionHost().run with expectHash, and forcing the flag back fails it (negative control).

value.text:
Review round 7 on PR #1680 head 21a6e6024 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, 3 findings; CodeRabbit full review, 3 findings plus a scope note), verified.
- (Codex P1) An SDK close retry now carries every expectation the active scopes hold on the tracker (activeItemRevisionExpectations), so a guard on a dependent the close would auto-unblock survives. Guards from scopes bound to other trackers are never included.
- (Codex P2) closeRetryScopePrefix in main.ts decides from the final tracker value of a marked bootstrap parse, so a non-empty --pm-path followed by --pm-path= is handled.
- (Codex P2) A refusal already rendered for its own invocation is marked (global registry, kept through the cause chain), and enclosing scopes on the same tracker keep that rendering. An inner client's --no-extensions therefore survives.
- (CodeRabbit) At the extension-override bind site, the recovery takes path and noExtensions from the typed bootstrap parse. Output flags still come from the full parse, because the bootstrap parse does not see command-position --json.
- (CodeRabbit) required and next_steps of a strict close refusal stay truthful when the CLI withdraws the retry (close-task): record the evidence with next_best_command, then repeat the original command.
- (CodeRabbit) withExpectedItemRevisions with a pmRoot-only context renders the resolved root.
Not changed: CodeRabbit's out-of-scope note on pm-gh1678, pm-gh1679 and pm-t5gari. This repository requires a pm item for every new GitHub issue and lands tracker changes through a reviewed PR.

Review round 8 on PR #1680 head 844e222d6 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, 2 findings, verified and fixed).
(1) An embedded CLI run inside an SDK guard dropped that guard: the argv-based repair replaced the producer retry, which carried it. The CLI repair now appends any --expect-hash=<id>=<hash> guard from the producer retry that the caller did not type (as a bare hash, <id>=<hash>, or either attached).
(2) Nested scopes expecting different revisions of one item would yield a retry that always fails with expected_revision_duplicate. activeItemRevisionExpectations now returns undefined for that case, and the producer withdraws the CLI retry with SDK-only guidance, as it does for lifecyclePolicy overrides.
Specs: the out-of-band guard (unit and an embedded CLI run inside PmClient.withExpectedItemRevisions) and conflicting nested guards. Lint, the static gate and 157 targeted specs pass. The local full coverage run was stopped by the host for low memory; CI coverage covers it.

value.text: Codex review round 12 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) on 1f14c6602: itemRevisionRefusalTracker and isItemRevisionRefusalScoped read each error's cause before knowing it was a revision refusal, so an unrelated SDK callback error whose cause getter throws was replaced by the getter's exception (withExpectedItemRevisions rejected with the wrong error). Both now walk one bounded refusalCauseChain generator that ends the chain when a cause accessor throws. Regression in item-revision.spec.ts (the opaque error is rejected as itself); dropping the try/catch fails it with Error: cause accessor.

value.text: Round 14, Greptile P2 on f71fd6464 (src/cli/expected-revisions.ts:45), confirmed and fixed. With PM_PATH set and a typed whitespace-only tracker (--pm-path ' ' or --pm-path='  '), resolvePmRoot trims the value and writes through PM_PATH. invocationRevisionRecovery passed the raw value to resolvePmCommandScopeArgs, whose 'requested || environment' check took the whitespace as an explicit selection, so the stale-revision reads named --pm-path ' '. Replayed without the original PM_PATH they read the cwd tracker. resolvePmCommandScopeArgs (src/sdk/command-line.ts) now treats a blank typed tracker like an omitted one and names the environment's tracker; non-blank spellings are kept verbatim. Regressions: the integration spec runs both blank spellings from inside a workspace whose own tracker holds the same id. The prescribed reads name ../.agents/pm and return the decoy item at the guard's current revision. A direct unit test covers undefined, empty, space and tab-space values, plus a padded explicit path kept verbatim. Negative control: with the old expression restored the unit test fails with [--pm-path, ' '] in place of [--pm-path, ../.agents/pm]. The close-retry scope (closeRetryScopePrefix) already handled this composition in round 11 and is unchanged.
